findings.summary: Binding the month axis as EXACTDATE(<calculated date field>) writes an instance Tableau cannot resolve; every sheet in the workbook then renders empty on Cloud (observed: all three replica sheets blank, replica CSV 0 bytes).
findings.workaround: Use the native MONTHTRUNC(<raw date field>) derivation instead, which is what the author's workbook stores ([tmn:Order Date:qk]).

findings.summary: A configure_custom_tooltip run that references EXACTDATE(<date field>) makes Tableau Cloud render the entire worksheet empty (batch-17 ww20/ww28 finding).
findings.workaround: Reference the bare date field in tooltip runs; the tooltip then shows month granularity, a text-only difference.

findings.summary: A quantitative field placed first on a layered row shelf emits its own axis (nested with '*') instead of nesting under the row dimension, so the hidden Sort key must be declared field_type='ordinal'.
findings.workaround: Declare the sort key as discrete ordinal and keep the measures in a single trailing group, matching the author's ((Sort / (Sub / Longest)) * (Sales + Peak)).
